title: Token entropy bucketizer and latency-cost model exporter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a streaming job that computes privacy-friendly token-entropy buckets and joins short-term latency signals to produce a compact exported table used by billing attribution and the cost-model trainer. The goal is twofold: 1) create a lower-cardinality per-tenant/route representation of token composition so downstream billing jobs can attribute cost with bounded error, and 2) emit a summarized latency-cost feature bundle to the model team for unit-cost prediction. This reduces load on the existing per-event reconciler by pre-aggregating high-cardinality dimensions and enables transparent, auditable exports for invoicing and cost-analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming job deployed to staging and producing daily and billing-window aggregates to BigQuery with agreed schema
Aggregate-level token-entropy error <= 2% (95th percentile tenants) vs. gold replay baseline in test harness
End-to-end processing lag from event arrival to exported row < 5 minutes for 99th percentile during normal traffic
Graceful fallback: when late events arrive beyond the window, they are routed to the existing reconciliation path without double-counting
Runbook and dashboard created; on-call SLO for export freshness added to console-2026.03 release notes
tasks: Design schema for entropy_bucket key (tenant, route, model_variant, time_bucket) and export flat table
Prototype bucketing algorithm (count-min sketch + reservoir sampling) and evaluate memory/accuracy trade-offs
Implement Flink stateful stream job with event-time windowing and late-arrival policy
Add deterministic hashing for privacy-preserving bucketing and config knobs for bucket granularity
Integrate with existing token event producer (kafka topic: tokens.events.v2) and add consumer offset tracking
Create BigQuery export pipeline and rollout canary wiring for 10% of tenants
E2E validation: test-harness replay, compare against ledger-based reconciler, produce discrepancy report
Docs: runbook, schema spec, PRD links, and billing-team handoff
updates: 2026-02-10 - Ticket created by Aisha Patel: initial problem statement and success metrics. Linked to ENG-31208 (prefix reconciliation work).

2026-02-17 - Prototype complete: small Python simulation comparing simple bucketing vs. CMS+reservoir; memory vs. error curves attached. Decision: CMS alone underestimates tail token variety; combined approach chosen.

2026-02-25 - Design review with PM (Ravi Shah) and SRE (Elena Garcia). Action: add deterministic salt per-tenant for hashing and add a noise clamp to limit re-identification risk. SRE requested an explicit backpressure path for Kafka lag > 2 minutes.

2026-03-03 - Implementation started (Marcus Nguyen). Flink topology created with keyed state and RocksDB checkpoints. Initial CI job failing due to state restore mismatch; Ivan Petrov opened a PR to normalize serializer versions (GH: redwood/inference#8762).

2026-03-08 - Shadow run in staging: consumed 48h of traffic at 5% of production load. Observed 1.8% aggregate error and 3.2m 95p latency—within targets. Noted CPU hotspot in serializer path; profiling ticket ENG-631002 created.

2026-03-12 - Blocker found: BigQuery quota for streaming inserts in customer project exceeded for export schema. Eng ops requested quota increase; temporary mitigation: switch to batched export every 3 minutes. Hold on 75% canary rollout until quota confirmed.
tech_decisions: Use Flink for stateful streaming (event-time semantics) instead of batch Spark to meet freshness SLOs
Combine Count-Min Sketch for frequent tokens with reservoir sampling for per-tenant tail representativeness
Deterministic tenant salt for bucket hashing to support reproducible aggregation and controlled PII risk
Export at billing-window granularity with optional sub-window snapshots for debugging; primary export target is BigQuery
When BigQuery streaming quota is constrained, fall back to micro-batched GCS newline-delimited JSON uploads and a load job
test_plan: Unit tests for CMS and reservoir modules with synthetic token distributions
Integration tests: local Flink job against a recorded kafka replay (48h traffic sample)
Staging shadow run: 5% traffic for 72h, compare export against gold ledger for billing deltas and flag >1% discrepancies
Canary rollout: 10% tenants for 7 days with automated alerting on exporter lag and delta drift >2%
Post-rollout audit: cross-validate first two invoices produced with existing reconciler and record any adjustments
